advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide explicitly how idle_sync should treat unpushed_count=="unknown" (push-anyway or log at WARNING) instead of silently equating it with an empty backlog.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/sync.py:321: `if was_pending or push_state.unpushed_count(tracker, remote_ref) not in ("0", "unknown"):`
push_state.unpushed_count returns "unknown" on any rev-list failure: src/rebar/_store/push_state.py:60-64 `if res.returncode != 0 or not count.isdigit(): return "unknown"`

_report_idle_outcome then logs "current" at DEBUG when not pending (src/rebar/_store/sync.py:342), so an unmeasurable backlog is reported as a healthy/quiet server — the check cannot distinguish 'checked and clean' from 'the count instrument failed'.
advisory.finding: In idle_sync, when push_state.unpushed_count returns "unknown" (a transient git error reading the backlog) and the marker is not pending, the push is skipped and the run logs "current" at DEBUG — a backlog that could not be measured is indistinguishable from an empty backlog, so a genuine fork can stay unpushed and invisible on the very path meant to heal it.
scenarios: A transient git error (e.g. rev-list fails under load or a brief FS issue) makes unpushed_count return 'unknown' while HEAD is actually ahead of the remote and no pending marker exists.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pass the (branch, remote) already resolved inside _reconverge through to idle_sync instead of re-reading with a hard-coded fallback.
evidence: Reaching line 308 requires status=='done', which in _reconverge means _store_destination already returned non-None (src/rebar/_store/sync.py:256-259), so the fallback is dead code that masks any later config-read failure by substituting defaults rather than skipping.
advisory.finding: idle_sync re-reads the store destination with a hard-coded fallback `or ("tickets", "origin")` after _reconverge already returned a non-skip status; the fallback is unreachable on the happy path and, if it ever did fire, would compute remote_ref against the wrong remote/branch and push/diagnose against a bogus ref.
scenarios: Store config becomes unreadable between _reconverge and this second read (rare race); the code then proceeds with remote_ref 'origin/tickets' regardless of the store's actual configured remote/branch.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that run_idle_sync_loop propagates RemovedInputError raised by sync_fn instead of logging-and-continuing.
evidence: test_mcp_idle_sync.py:205-208 injects `OSError("disk went away")` — the broad-except branch, not the RemovedInputError branch.
Named violating input: a sync_fn that raises RemovedInputError must cause run_idle_sync_loop to propagate (not log-and-continue); this is unexercised behaviorally.
src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:353-354 (docstring contract): 'Each run holds the drain gauge, so a SIGTERM drain waits for a push in progress rather than exiting under it.'
test_mcp_idle_sync.py:223-224: `gauge.begin_draining()` is called before the loop runs, so the first `gauge.draining` check returns immediately and no run ever holds the gauge.
Named violating sequence: draining begins while sync_fn is mid-execution holding the gauge — the gauge must read non-zero (drain waits) until that run's finally-release; unexercised.
advisory.finding: The newly-added RemovedInputError re-raise in run_idle_sync_loop (the loop must propagate RemovedInputError rather than swallow-and-retry like other exceptions) has no behavioral test. test_a_failing_run_is_logged_and_the_next_tick_still_runs injects OSError, which exercises the swallow/retry path, not the re-raise path. The only RemovedInputError coverage for this module is the source-text structural grep in test_tombstone_registry, which cannot detect that the loop's runtime behavior actually propagates.
merged_from: The stated contract 'each run holds the drain gauge, so a SIGTERM drain waits for a push in progress rather than exiting under it' is not tested. test_the_loop_stops_once_the_server_is_draining calls begin_draining() BEFORE any run starts, so it only covers the pre-hold early-exit; no test exercises draining arriving WHILE a run holds the gauge and asserts the drain observes a non-zero gauge until the in-flight run releases.
scenarios: A refactor reorders the except clauses so `except Exception` swallows RemovedInputError, silently retrying a retired load-bearing input every tick — the structural grep still passes because the text is present.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test passing sync_fn that raises rebar._deprecations.RemovedInputError and asserting pytest.raises(RemovedInputError) out of run_idle_sync_loop, and that calls was length 1 (no retry).

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that run() starts the idle sync for transport==http and skips it for transport==stdio.
evidence: Search for `transport == "http"` in tests returns only tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py:89 (an unrelated config assertion); no test calls run()/the gate and asserts start_idle_sync is invoked for http and skipped for stdio.
Named violating inputs: cfg.mcp.transport == "stdio" must NOT start the idle sync; cfg.mcp.transport == "http" must start it — neither branch is driven.
blocking.finding: The newly-added transport gate in run() (`if cfg.mcp.transport == "http": start_idle_sync(...)`) has no test: neither the http branch (idle sync IS started) nor the stdio branch (idle sync is NOT started) is exercised. A regression flipping the condition, dropping the guard, or inverting it would not be caught.
scenarios: A refactor drops or inverts the http gate and a stdio per-session process starts a permanent idle loop, or an http server silently never syncs (the exact 50-minute-fork regression this change fixes).
blocking.suggested_fix: Add a unit test that invokes the run() wiring (or a thin helper around the gate) with a stubbed cfg.mcp.transport of 'http' and 'stdio', patching start_idle_sync, and asserting it is called exactly once for http and not at all for stdio.
